_doc: Goya · prologue: four docent cards, each voiced by one line from a later letter. Spanish = modern spelling (accents, b/v, h, x/j, joined words; no rewording and no change of word order), each message keeps the text as printed in the public-domain edition in orig.es (shown in the app as an optional ‘original spelling’ line). Editors' interjections are removed; nothing is taken from the 1981/82 or 2003 editions or their notes. verified=false: checked against the archive.org full text, a last check against the page images is still to do. en · ko translated from the Spanish for this app. Replies and talks are written by this app, not by the recipients.

letters.dateNote: The date is his birth at Fuendetodos (30 March 1746; baptism record printed in Beruete 1916, p. 3), the start of the period this card covers. The words come from a later letter to Martín Zapater, 9 January 1779 (Beruete 1916, p. 10).
letters.ref: Beruete 1916, p. 10 · A. de Beruete y Moret, Goya, pintor de retratos (Madrid, 1916), p. 10 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/AV192

heading.en: A child of a dry village
heading.es: Un niño de un pueblo seco

body.ko: 1746년 3월 30일, 아라곤의 메마른 산골 마을 푸엔데토도스에서 태어났어요. 아버지 호세는 사라고사의 도금 장인이었고, 마을에는 어머니 그라시아 루시엔테스의 집안이 있었어요. 어린 시절은 사라고사에서 보냈어요. 어른이 된 고야는 어릴 적 친구 마르틴에게 쓴 편지마다 ‘작은 밭과 좋은 삶’을 꿈꿨어요.
body.en: He was born on 30 March 1746 in Fuendetodos, a dry hill village in Aragon. His father José was a master gilder in Zaragoza; his mother Gracia Lucientes came from a family of the village. He grew up in Zaragoza. As a grown man, in letter after letter to his childhood friend Martín, Goya dreamed of ‘a few little fields and a good life’.

source.en: Years later, to Martín from Madrid · 9 January 1779

messages.es: Pero, chiquío, campicos y buena vida: nadie me sacará de esta opinión.
messages.en: But, my boy, a few little fields and a good life: no one will talk me out of that.
messages.ko: 그래도 친구야, 작은 밭 몇 뙈기에 좋은 삶이면 돼. 누구도 내 이 생각은 못 바꿔.

orig.es: Pero chiquio campicos y buena vida, nadie me sacará de esta opinión

messages.source: A. de Beruete y Moret, Goya, pintor de retratos (Madrid, 1916), p. 10 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/AV192

speak.es: Pero, / chiquío, / campicos y buena vida: // nadie me sacará de esta opinión.
speak.en: But, / my boy, / a few little fields and a good life: // no one will talk me out of that.
speak.ko: 그래도 친구야, / 작은 밭 몇 뙈기에 좋은 삶이면 돼. // 누구도 내 이 생각은 못 바꿔.

note.ko: ‘캄피코스(campicos)’는 ‘작은 밭’을 귀엽게 부르는 아라곤 말투예요. ‘치키오(chiquío)’는 ‘얘야, 이 친구야’ 하고 다정하게 부르는 말이에요.
note.en: ‘Campicos’ is an affectionate Aragonese way of saying ‘little fields’; ‘chiquío’ is a fond ‘my boy, my friend’.
note.source: A. de Beruete y Moret, Goya, pintor de retratos (Madrid, 1916), p. 10 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/AV192 ; image: see plate.imageSource

why.ko: 훗날 고야가 왕궁 태피스트리 밑그림으로 그린 아라곤 같은 들판의 여름이에요. 편지 속 ‘작은 밭과 좋은 삶’이 이런 모습이었을 거예요.
why.en: A summer harvest Goya later painted as a tapestry cartoon for the royal palace: the kind of fields he means by ‘a few little fields and a good life’.

letters.dateNote: About 1760: his school years at the Escuelas Pías in Zaragoza, where he met Martín Zapater (approximate). The words come from a later letter to Martín, 28 November 1787 (Zapater y Gómez, p. 23).
letters.ref: Zapater y Gómez, p. 23 · F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 23 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa

heading.es: Martín, el amigo de la escuela

body.ko: 사라고사의 에스쿠엘라스 피아스(피아리스트 수도회 학교)에서 글을 배웠어요. 그곳에서 평생의 벗 마르틴 사파테르를 만났어요. 열서너 살 무렵부터 화가 호세 루산의 화실에서 그림을 배웠고, 마드리드 왕립 아카데미의 장학 공모에는 1763년과 1766년 두 번 떨어졌어요.
body.en: He learned his letters at the Escuelas Pías, the Piarist school in Zaragoza, and there met his lifelong friend Martín Zapater. From the age of about thirteen he trained in the studio of the painter José Luzán; he twice failed the Royal Academy's scholarship competitions in Madrid, in 1763 and 1766.

source.en: Years later, to Martín from Madrid · 28 November 1787

messages.es: …tal vez tú te conservarás como en la escuela del P. Joaquín.
messages.en: …perhaps you are still just as you were at Father Joaquín's school.
messages.ko: …너는 아마 호아킨 신부님 학교에 다니던 그때 그대로겠지.

orig.es: tal bez tu te conserbaras como en la escuela del P. Joaquín

messages.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 23 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa

speak.es: …tal vez tú te conservarás como en la escuela del P. Joaquín.
speak.en: …perhaps you are still just as you were at Father Joaquín's school.
speak.ko: …너는 아마 호아킨 신부님 학교에 다니던 그때 그대로겠지.

note.ko: 마흔한 살의 고야가 ‘나는 주름투성이 늙은이가 됐는데, 너는 학교 때 그대로겠지’ 하고 농담하던 편지의 끝 구절이에요. P.는 신부님(Padre)의 줄임이에요.
note.en: The end of a letter in which Goya, at forty-one, jokes that he has grown old and wrinkled while Martín must be just as he was at school. ‘P.’ stands for Padre, Father.
note.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 23 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa ; image: see plate.imageSource

letters.dateNote: 1771: Italy and the competition of the Parma Academy (the month of his journey is not known). The words come from a later letter to Martín, 25 July 1781 (Zapater y Gómez, p. 9).
letters.ref: Zapater y Gómez, p. 9 · F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa

heading.es: Al otro lado de los Alpes

body.ko: 스물네 살 무렵 이탈리아로 건너가 그림을 공부했어요. 1771년 파르마 아카데미 공모전에 〈알프스에서 처음 이탈리아를 내려다보는 승리자 한니발〉을 냈고, 1등은 못 했지만 심사에서 좋은 평을 받았어요. 그해 사라고사로 돌아와 필라르 대성당의 작은 천장화를 맡았어요.
body.en: At about twenty-four he went to Italy to study painting. In 1771 he sent ‘Hannibal the Conqueror Viewing Italy from the Alps’ to the competition of the Parma Academy; it did not win first prize but was praised by the jury. That year he returned to Zaragoza and was given a small ceiling to paint in the basilica of the Pilar.

source.en: Years later, to Martín from Madrid · 25 July 1781

messages.es: …pues parece que Dios se ha acordado de mí.
messages.en: …for it seems that God has remembered me.

orig.es: pues parece que Dios se a acordado de mi

messages.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa

speak.es: …pues parece que Dios se ha acordado de mí.
speak.en: …for it seems that God has remembered me.

note.ko: 이 말은 열 해 뒤, 마드리드의 큰 성당 제단화를 맡게 되었을 때 쓴 편지의 한 구절이에요. 이탈리아에서 돌아온 젊은 화가에게 그런 날은 아직 멀었어요.
note.en: These words come from a letter written ten years later, when he was chosen to paint an altarpiece for a great Madrid church; for the young painter just back from Italy, that day was still far off.
note.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa ; image: see plate.imageSource

letters.dateNote: The date is his wedding to Josefa Bayeu in Madrid (25 July 1773). The words come from a later letter to Martín, 9 August 1780 (Zapater y Gómez, p. 11), the same sentence as chapter I, letter 7.
letters.ref: Zapater y Gómez, p. 11 · F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 11 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa

body.ko: 1773년 7월 25일 마드리드에서, 궁정 화가 프란시스코 바예우의 누이동생 호세파 바예우와 결혼했어요. 바예우는 고야의 손위 처남이자 스승 같은 사람이 되었어요. 1774년 말 고야는 마드리드로 불려 가, 왕립 태피스트리 공장에서 짤 그림의 밑그림을 그리게 되었어요.
body.en: On 25 July 1773, in Madrid, he married Josefa Bayeu, the younger sister of the court painter Francisco Bayeu, who became his brother-in-law and something of a master to him. At the end of 1774 Goya was called to Madrid to paint cartoons for the Royal Tapestry Factory.

source.en: Years later, to Martín from Madrid · 9 August 1780

messages.es: Mi mujer te lo estima infinito.
messages.en: My wife is ever so grateful to you for it.

orig.es: Mi mujer te lo estima infinito

messages.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 11 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa

speak.es: Mi mujer te lo estima infinito.
speak.en: My wife is ever so grateful to you for it.

note.ko: 고야는 편지에서 아내를 늘 ‘내 아내(mi mujer)’라고 불러요. 호세파가 마르틴에게 고마워한 일은 I장의 마지막 편지에 나와요.
note.en: In his letters Goya always calls her ‘mi mujer’, my wife. What Josefa thanks Martín for comes in the last letter of chapter I.
note.source: F. Zapater y Gómez, Goya. Noticias biográficas (Zaragoza, 1868 text; scan without imprint), p. 11 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyanoticiasbibl00zapa ; image: see plate.imageSource
